newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures end with weather gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures end with weather gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, boosted by the season's first real cold snap, ended higher across the board Monday in lackluster trade, but gains were modest and prices remained in recent technical ranges.
December climbed 6.4 cents to close at $2.733 per million British thermal units. January settled up the same amount at $2.739. Other deferreds ended up by one to 7.8 cents.

"It was a weather-driven rally but there are still plenty of skeptics. There's some warmer weather coming in behind it," said one East Coast trader, adding December needed to close above $2.75 to really get the bulls excited.
While some cold weather this week and an uncertain winter ahead were likely to keep the bears guarded near-term, traders noted little conviction among the bulls.
"It's a little too early to be a big bull or bear. There's enough uncertainty (about winter) to warrant these prices, but no one's getting crazy," a trader said.
Technically, traders said recent ranges were intact, with December resistance still at $2.745 and then at the $2.88 contract high. Key support was still in the $2.52-2.53 area.

Cash sources said Gulf Coast prices firmed slightly Monday to the low-$2.70s. Midwest prices also were modestly higher in the low-$2.60s. Cold Northeast weather this week drove New York city gate gas prices up another dime or more to the high-$3.20s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip rose 3.6 cents to $2.207. NYMEX said 25,438 Hub contracts traded, up only slightly from Friday's revised tally of 25,100.
NYMEX December Alberta natgas closed one cent higher at a new contract high of $1.30, while deferreds settled mixed. NYMEX said three Alberta contracts traded versus no trading on Friday.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded for the third consecutive day. December ended unchanged at $2.49.

On the KCBT, December finished five cents higher at $2.535, while deferreds settled up by one to four cents. The December East/West spread widened by 1.4 cents to 19.8 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 69 contracts traded, up from Friday's total of 31.
